prompt: Two solid spheres, P and Q, have identical outer diameters and smooth surfaces. Sphere P is made of solid lead and sphere Q is made of hollow plastic. Both spheres are dropped simultaneously from rest from a high altitude in still air. Which statement correctly compares their motion?
options: Sphere P reaches a higher terminal velocity than sphere Q.
Sphere Q reaches a higher terminal velocity than sphere P.
Both spheres reach the exact same terminal velocity at the same time.
Sphere Q experiences a larger air resistance than sphere P at any given speed.

answer.explanation: Because both spheres have identical dimensions, they experience the same drag force at any given speed. However, sphere P has a much larger mass and weight. To balance this larger weight, sphere P must accelerate to a higher speed before drag equals weight.

distractor_explanations: Correct: sphere P has greater weight, requiring a larger drag force and therefore a higher speed to achieve D = mg.
The lighter sphere Q reaches force equilibrium at a lower speed, so its terminal velocity is lower.
Terminal velocity depends on weight when shapes and sizes are equal; lead has much greater weight.
Drag force depends on size, shape, and speed, which are identical for both spheres at any specified speed.
hints: Compare the drag forces on both spheres at the same speed.
What condition must be met for each sphere to reach terminal velocity?
solution: Option 1 is correct. Identical shape and size mean identical D(v). But W_lead > W_plastic, so D must become larger to balance W_lead, which requires a higher terminal speed.
teacher_walkthrough: Step 1: Identical geometry means both spheres experience identical drag force D at any speed v.
Step 2: Sphere P has higher density, so m_P > m_Q, meaning W_P > W_Q.
Step 3: Terminal velocity requires D = W.
Step 4: Sphere P requires larger D, so it must reach a higher terminal speed.
